title: Lumina - embeddings & rerank discovery
summary: Initial discovery to understand Lumina's retrieval + rerank use case: ingesting user docs, vector DB choices, throughput targets for search and rerank, and security/compliance constraints. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for embedding generation and on-the-fly reranking (cross-encoder). Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, security docs, and propose PoC scope with a 2-week pilot to validate latency and cost for 200 QPS hybrid workload.
topics: hybrid search: BM25 + vector + cross-encoder rerank
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
security: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark template and suggested dataset slice (Maya)
Redwood to share SOC 2 + security pack and KMS integration notes (Carlos)
Lumina to provide representative dataset sample and expected query distribution (Jenna)
Schedule PoC kickoff (2 weeks) to validate 200 QPS hybrid search and top-k rerank latency (all)
Follow-up call to review benchmarks and pricing for Dedicated capacity (1 week)
action_items: Maya Chen: Send benchmark template and example scripts (due: 2026-03-18)
Carlos Ruiz: Package security docs + KMS/HSM notes (due: 2026-03-17)
Jenna Park: Share 10k doc sample + query distribution CSV (due: 2026-03-19)
Tom Nguyen: Confirm internal vector DB choices and current infra (Milvus) (due: 2026-03-20)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Jenna (Lumina Head of ML), Raj (Lumina CTO), Tom (Lumina Eng Manager)

Summary: quick discovery on embeddings -> rerank. focus on vector DB integration, throughput and whether to use hosted vs dedicated vs private for embedding gen and reranker latency.

00:00:05 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick intros?
00:00:12 Jenna (Lumina): Hey Maya, Jenna here, head of ML at Lumina. We run a search product over large user documents, looking to improve relevance with embeddings + reranking.
00:00:20 Raj (Lumina): Raj here, CTO, I'll be focused on infra and security constraints.
00:00:24 Tom (Lumina): Tom, eng manager, we'll own integration.
00:00:28 Carlos (Redwood): Hi all, Carlos from Redwood, I'll cover performance and architecture.
00:00:33 Maya (Redwood): Awesome. Quick objective for today: understand current stack, throughput expectations, success criteria, and constraints so we can propose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and a PoC.

00:01:02 Jenna: Great. Current stack: we ingest support docs and product docs into a Milvus cluster right now. We generate embeddings with an in-house model right now but it's costly; we're evaluating managed embedding generation. Our query load is spiky - avg 80 QPS peak 200 QPS during business hours. Typical top-k retrieval is 100 then we do a cross-encoder rerank for top 10. Latency SLO for end-to-end search around 350ms 95th currently it's a bit higher.

00:01:42 Raj: On security we need SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and prefer VPC peering for any hosted services. Data residency is US only for now.

00:01:55 Carlos: Thanks - that helps. Quick clarifying Qs: When you say you do cross-encoder rerank for top 10, is that a transformer-based cross-encoder running per query? And where is that hosted today?
00:02:07 Jenna: Yes, it's a transformer reranker - currently running on a small GPU pool in-house. It's the costliest piece so we'd like to see if Redwood can help with model hosting and lower per-query cost.

00:02:18 Maya: Understood. We typically advise two patterns: 1) Redwood for embedding generation + customer vector DB (so you keep Milvus) and Redwood for optional rerank via hosted inferencing; or 2) Redwood Dedicated/Private to host both tokenization/embeddings and the reranker, and optionally store embeddings in Redwood-managed storage if you want simplified ops. Both have tradeoffs.

00:02:45 Tom: If we keep Milvus, how does Redwood integrate? Any SDKs or connectors?
00:02:50 Carlos: We have SDKs and examples for Pinecone, Milvus and Weaviate. Integration is straightforward: call Redwood embeddings endpoint to produce vectors (you can batch), then upsert into Milvus. For rerank, you can either pull top-k from Milvus and call Redwood's reranker endpoint (cross-encoder) to re-score, or host reranker on Dedicated nodes for lower latency.

00:03:20 Raj: Latency is the big one - currently pull from Milvus is ~30ms, rerank on our GPU is ~150-200ms per query which is the pain. If we move rerank to Redwood Hosted, what's typical latency?
00:03:33 Carlos: For Hosted, cross-encoder latency depends on model size and batch. For a medium cross-encoder (base-sized) 10 items, typically 60-120ms per request under normal load. For consistent sub-100ms 95p at 200 QPS you'd likely want Dedicated capacity or specialized lower-latency model variants. Also keep in mind batching helps throughput but adds a bit to tail latency.

00:03:58 Jenna: What about dimensionality? Our current embeddings are 512d and we're debating switching to 1536d for better recall. Cost and storage go up though. Thoughts?
00:04:08 Carlos: Tradeoff: higher dims usually buy recall but increase storage and nearest-neighbor compute. If you use IVF/HNSW in Milvus it's manageable but nearest neighbor search time and memory grows. One pattern is to use 512d for initial retrieval, then apply a denser 1536d embedding for rerank or only for cold docs. Another is hybrid search - BM25 + 512d vector - to keep cost down. We can help benchmark 512 vs 1536 on your dataset.

00:04:40 Tom: Hybrid search - how do you typically combine BM25 and vector scores? Any recommended normalization?
00:04:46 Carlos: Usually normalize scores and tune a weighted sum; some teams do separate thresholds: use BM25 top 100 then vector top 100 then union and rerank. There's no one-size-fits-all; it'll depend on your query distribution. We'll give you an eval harness in the benchmark template.

00:05:10 Raj: On deployment: If we go Dedicated, do we get reserved GPUs inside Redwood infra? And how much ops does Redwood handle?
00:05:18 Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity - predictable throughput, data isolation, and SLA-backed targets. You get reserved GPU pools, autoscaling policies you configure, and Redwood manages the serving runtime. For private deployment (VPC or on-prem), the control plane can be customer-managed and you retain more network isolation (VPC peering or on-prem package). Dedicated sits between Hosted and Private for control vs ops responsibility.

00:05:45 Jenna: What about costs? Rough order of magnitude for 200 QPS hybrid with top-10 rerank?
00:05:51 Carlos: Cost varies a lot by model and deployment. Very rough: Hosted embeddings + Hosted rerank for 200 QPS could be high unless you tune to smaller models and batching. Dedicated reserved GPUs amortize cost better. We'll put some sample pricing scenarios in the follow-up. The PoC will surface more accurate numbers.

00:06:15 Tom: For the reranker, is it always a cross-encoder? Could we do a two-stage pointwise model that's cheaper?
00:06:21 Carlos: Yes, alternatives exist: bi-encoder re-ranking or learned reweighing can be cheaper. Cross-encoders give best quality but cost more. A common approach: use bi-encoder + lightweight classifier for 2nd stage, reserve cross-encoder for a final personalization pass or critical flows. We'll help lay out tradeoffs in the PoC.

00:06:45 Jenna: We also care about cold-start indexing velocity - how fast can we re-embed and upsert 1M docs?

00:06:51 Carlos: For bulk embedding gen, you can use Redwood batch endpoints and parallel workers. Rough numbers: with dedicated capacity you can sustain many thousands of embeddings/sec depending on model size and GPU. For example, a mid-sized embedding model on a dedicated GPU can do ~1500-3000 1536-d embeddings/sec. We'll provide more detailed throughput expected in the template.

00:07:20 Raj: On security - KMS integration for customer-managed keys is critical. How is data at rest handled if we use Hosted?

00:07:27 Maya: For Hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit; for customer-managed keys we support KMS integrations in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we also have enterprise options for key control - we'll include the exact limitations in the security pack. Audit logs and SSO/SAML are supported for enterprise accounts.

00:07:47 Tom: Any concerns about PII? We have some user-submitted docs with sensitive fields.

00:07:50 Carlos: We recommend redaction pipeline before embeddings where possible. For Hosted, you can turn on retention policies and logging and route sensitive workloads to Dedicated/Private so that data doesn't persist in shared environments.

00:08:05 Jenna: Ok good. For vector DB choices, you mentioned connectors for Milvus. Do you recommend moving to Pinecone or staying with Milvus?

00:08:12 Carlos: Both fine. Pinecone is managed and reduces ops; Milvus gives more flexibility and can run on-prem. If you need on-prem or strict VPC-only access, Milvus + Dedicated/Private Redwood is a good combo. Pinecone tends to have optimized per-query latencies out of the box which helps tail latency for retrieval. We'll run benchmarks against Milvus in your environment as part of the PoC.

00:08:40 Raj: For the rerank cost, could you share ballpark per-call cost differences between Hosted and Dedicated?

00:08:47 Carlos: Ballpark: Hosted per-request cost accounts for multi-tenant overhead; Dedicated has fixed infra costs but lower marginal per-inference cost at scale. If you're sustaining 200 QPS, Dedicated almost always becomes more economical for cross-encoder workloads, especially if re-use and batching are possible. We'll illustrate with numbers in the pricing scenarios.

00:09:12 Maya: Quick check - success criteria for PoC? Jenna?

00:09:16 Jenna: Hit 95p end-to-end under 350ms for 200 QPS hybrid search including rerank; show relevance improvement on our eval set (NDCG up vs baseline); and cost per query less than our current in-house spend.

00:09:29 Maya: Great. We'll design PoC around those.

00:09:33 Tom: Operationally, how do rollouts work? Canary? A/B?

00:09:38 Carlos: We support canary rollouts and A/B, and can route traffic by policy. For rerank you can do shadow traffic to measure quality before switching. Also tracing hooks to tie model outputs back to routes in the Console.

00:09:52 Raj: Any questions from me: SSO/SAML is necessary and we need RBAC per team. Also retention and e-discovery for audits.

00:10:01 Maya: Noted. Those are standard enterprise asks - security pack will cover them.

00:10:10 Jenna: A few technical Qs: 1) What's the recommended batch size for embeddings to keep latency low but throughput good? 2) For rerank, can you do multi-candidate batching across queries?

00:10:20 Carlos: 1) For embeddings, batch sizes of 64-512 depending on model give good throughput; smaller batches lower latency. 2) For rerank, yes - if you can assemble candidates across queries you can improve GPU utilization (multi-query batching), but that changes latency tradeoffs. We'll show examples in the benchmark scripts.

00:10:45 Maya: We're going to propose two PoC tracks: track A - Redwood Hosted embeddings + call-out rerank (fastest to start); track B - Dedicated capacity hosting reranker (for latency targets). We'll help you size both.

00:11:00 Jenna: Sounds good. Any gotchas with Milvus upsert patterns?

00:11:04 Carlos: Watch upsert concurrency and index build windows - we recommend incremental upserts and building indexes during low traffic. We'll include Milvus-specific guidance.

00:11:18 Tom: For the reranker model, can we bring our fine-tuned checkpoint to Redwood?

00:11:22 Maya: Yes, customers can bring custom models for Dedicated/Private; Hosted has more restrictions but we can usually run customer checkpoints on Dedicated. We'll detail that in the PoC proposal.

00:11:35 Raj: What about logging and observability for requests down to token cost?

00:11:40 Carlos: Console gives per-route token cost, latency histograms, per-request traces and error analytics. We'll demo that in the follow-up.

00:11:52 Jenna: Are there any reference customers with similar scale and hybrid rerank flows?

00:11:56 Maya: We have a couple of mid-market companies using Milvus + Redwood rerank and one larger marketplace using dedicated rerank for low-latency checkout search; we'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up.

00:12:12 Tom: For the PoC data pipeline - recommended flow?

00:12:16 Carlos: Ingest -> preprocess/redact -> embed via Redwood batch -> upsert to Milvus -> serve retrieval -> call Redwood rerank endpoint (or Dedicated rerank) -> return results. We'll provide scripts.

00:12:30 Jenna: Ok let's talk about evaluation: how will we measure NDCG improvements?

00:12:34 Carlos: We'll provide an eval harness that computes NDCG/precision@k over a labeled set and supports A/B comparisons between your current pipeline and Redwood variants. We'll also include latency and cost metrics.

00:12:48 Raj: Anything about model quantization and performance?

00:12:52 Carlos: Yes, quantized variants can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput at slight quality cost. For Dedicated we can run int8 or 4-bit quantized rerankers depending on compatibility. We'll recommend quantization for large cross-encoders if cost is a concern.

00:13:08 Jenna: If we do 1536d embeddings for recall, do you recommend storing both 512d and 1536d to save compute?

00:13:14 Carlos: Many teams store a single embedding and compute additional variants offline for cold docs. Storing two embeddings doubles storage but gives flexibility. Another pattern: store 512d for retrieval and regenerate 1536d for docs that need higher recall on demand or via batch offline. We'll help you evaluate storage cost vs recall lift.

00:13:38 Tom: One more infra Q: For Private/on-prem deployment, how disruptive is install and who handles upgrades?

00:13:45 Maya: For Private we provide an on-prem package; our solutions engineering team helps with install and upgrades can be managed by your team or via a customer-managed control plane that Redwood supports. We'll map out support levels in the proposal.

00:13:58 Jenna: Great. Anything else we should consider?

00:14:01 Carlos: We'll also look at caching opportunities - prefix/KV cache for frequent queries can massively reduce cost. If you have many repeated queries, caching will help the 95th.

00:14:12 Raj: Let's talk PoC specifics - timeframe and success criteria again?

00:14:16 Maya: Proposed 2-week PoC: Week 1 instrument embedding generation and retrieval, run benchmarks for 512 vs 1536 dims; Week 2 run hybrid search and rerank latency tests at scaled QPS and produce cost estimates and quality metrics. Success: 95p <350ms at 200 QPS and NDCG improvement on eval set.

00:14:38 Jenna: That timeline works. We'll get the sample dataset to you by end of this week.

00:14:43 Tom: On tickets and support during PoC - who do we contact?

00:14:46 Maya: Direct SE support from Carlos and AE support from me; we'll provide a slack channel for the PoC.

00:14:54 Raj: Any blockers we foresee?

00:14:56 Carlos: Possibly network/VPC peering setup if you want low-latency access to Milvus in your VPC; that'll take some infra coordination but is routine. Also dataset labeling for eval - if that isn't ready, we can use sampled queries.

00:15:12 Jenna: Sound good. Let's recap next steps.

00:15:15 Maya: Recap: we'll send benchmark template, security pack, PoC plan (2-week), and pricing scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated. Jenna to share dataset. Carlos to prepare Milvus connector docs.

00:15:28 Jenna: Perfect. Thanks all.

00:15:31 Raj: Thanks.

00:15:34 -- call wind-down, some small talk --

00:16:00 Maya: (off-record) Thanks again everyone, we'll follow up after we compile materials.

[Note: transcript contains typical speech disfluencies and minor auto-transcription errors. Some proper nouns may be slightly mis-spelled by auto-transcribe. Portions of technical details summarized above for clarity.]
